Hi all —

Quick prep notes for Thu’s session and a few local testing tips so Sam’s team can get unblocked: 

1) Auth & env
- For the POC use an API key: export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-test-xxxx
- For SAML/SSO we’ll demonstrate the short-lived token exchange (STS) — flow: IdP -> your infra issues assertion -> our token endpoint -> short-lived machine token. We’ll include the curl snippets.

2) Local quickstart (TypeScript) — minimal steps:
- cd typescript-sample
- npm install
- export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-test-xxxx
- node ./src/chat.ts --model redwood/longform-v1 --prompt-file examples/prompt.txt

Example tool-calling pattern (pseudo-TS):

const res = await redwood.chat.create({
  model: 'redwood/longform-v1',
  messages: [{role: 'user', content: 'Search KB for refund policy'}],
  structured_output: {
    type: 'tool_call',
    tools: ['kb_search']
  },
});

if (res.tool_call && res.tool_call.name === 'kb_search') {
  const args = res.tool_call.args; // { query: 'refund policy' }
  const hits = await localKB.search(args.query);
  // rerank with embeddings
  const queryEmbedding = await redwood.embeddings.create({model: 'redwood/emb-small', input: [args.query]});
}

3) Embeddings + reranker (Python)
- We include a simple script that builds embeddings for synthetic_docs.json and then runs cosine similarity to return top-k. Uses requests to call /embeddings endpoint and numpy for reranking.

4) Routing & latency notes
- For low-latency chat route traffic to regional endpoint us-west-2 and pin model variants (we’ll show how to set REDWOOD_BASE_URL).
- Use prefix caching for predictable prompts (we’ll demo with the prompt file).

5) Attachments / repo
- I attached the quickstart zip and SAML guide to the initial thread. The same content is in the GitHub link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-quickstart

If Sam can run the simple TS flow above and paste any errors here, I’ll triage before the call. Looking forward to Thu.

—Dylan
